title: Copying an icon puts its SVG on the clipboard too
goal: The icon epic promises that copying an icon puts the same clean SVG the export writes on the clipboard, so a paste into Figma, a browser tool or a code editor gives shapes, not pixels. Today Copy puts only a picture (and the measurement list) there. Add the SVG for vector documents, so pasting into an app that takes SVG gets the drawing while pasting into chat still gets the picture.
notes: Manager review 2026-10-08 of icon-svg: success line icon-export 3 (Copying an icon puts the same clean SVG on the clipboard) is not met. Copy is Sources/Photonz/EditorState.swift copyCompositeToClipboard (PNG, TIFF, then .string spec list when measurePanelEnabled) with CompositeCopy.representations (Sources/PhotonzCore/CompositeCopy.swift lines ~17-19). SVG writing: SVGExport / SVGHandoff (the web destination). Separate from the blocked copying-an-icon-carries-the-white-canvas-the-exp (whether the white canvas comes along); if that card is answered first, the SVG follows the same background answer. Related check: find-out-whether-the-redline-copy-pastes-as-a-pi (what Chromium takes when text and picture are both there).
acceptance: Copying on a document drawn in vector (an icon frame, drawn paths and shapes) puts the same SVG the Export sheet writes for the web on the clipboard as an SVG type, beside the PNG and TIFF that are there today
A screenshot, a photograph or a video copies exactly as today

Pasting into TextEdit and into a local web page that reads the clipboard (never a real web service) shows which type each one takes; the picture still wins where a picture is expected, and both results are in the audit

If putting the SVG markup on as plain text is the only way Figma or a code editor will take it, and that clashes with the measurement list text, the task opens a decision card on which text Copy carries instead of guessing
Tests first for the representation list (CompositeCopy); a walk at Next defaults draws a 24 unit icon, copies it and checks the clipboard holds the SVG with whole-unit coordinates
Try: New Frame, Icon 24, draw a circle, Command C, paste into a text editor that takes SVG. Audit written under queue/audits/
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task log if it does not

log.note: Pre-build review: Command C at Next defaults copies the PICKED layer, and after drawing, the circle is picked. So the SVG rides on the whole-picture copies (Shift Command C, Command C with nothing picked and no marquee) and on Command C with a frame picked (that frame's SVG, the same thing Export writes for it). A single picked shape gets none because Export never writes one. Photoshop has Copy SVG on a layer's right-click; that idea went into the follow-up card.

Measured with the real copy: Chrome 153 gives a page image/svg+xml and image/png (paste event and clipboard.read), and a contenteditable box takes the PNG. WebKit and NSTextView (rich and plain) never see the SVG type, and a textarea gets nothing. Markup as plain text is the only way into a code editor, and that slot holds the measurement list, so per the acceptance it went to a card on a follow-up task, an-icon-svg-pastes-into-a-code-editor (blocked on that card). The clipboard was saved and put back afterwards.

Rough items: the code editor gap became a task with a card; the white surface folds into copying-an-icon-carries-the-white-canvas-the-exp; the single-shape copy and the untried Figma/VS Code stay in this log and the audit.

Copy Merged, Command C with nothing picked and Command C on a picked frame now put the Export (web page) SVG on the clipboard as public.svg-image after PNG and TIFF. Screenshots, photos and videos are unchanged. Verified: CompositeCopy and SVGWholeUnits tests, full suite green (11,893 tests); copy-an-icon-as-svg-walk at Next defaults matches the copy byte for byte against writeSVG in whole units and checks a screenshot carries no SVG; Chrome 153, WebKit and NSTextView measured with the real copy (docs/design/references/svg-copy-check). Getting the SVG code into code editors as text is a card on an-icon-svg-pastes-into-a-code-editor. Audit queue/audits/2026-10-08-copy-an-icon-as-svg.json
